Budapest, Rio, Quito, Wembley, Lusail, and New Jersey were the settings for a story marked by tears, resignations, records, and a glory that took years to arrive.
articles.body:
L ionel Messi's first adventure with the Argentina National Team lasted just 47 seconds . The final performance will begin more than 21 years later, in front of a packed Monumental stadium and with a country ready to say goodbye. Between those two images fits practically an entire footballing life: defeats that seemed definitive, a resignation that shocked the world, nights of redemption and, finally, the scene that for years seemed impossible: Messi lifting the World Cup.

This Tuesday, against Benin, the number 10 will put on the albiceleste jersey for the last time. He arrives at his farewell with 207 matches, 125 goals, and 66 assists for the senior national team, according to the official AFA records. His participation in the tribute at the Monumental will bring his total to 208 appearances . An extraordinary figure, although insufficient to explain what happened over those more than two decades.

A beginning no one could have imagined

At 18, Messi had already given an early sign of the footballer he could become by taking part in the 2005 U-20 World Cup. He scored six goals, netted Argentina's two in the final against Nigeria, and finished the tournament with the Golden Boot and the Golden Ball.

On August 17, 2005, just a few weeks after taking part with the Under-20 team, he made his debut for the senior national team against Hungary in Budapest. José Pekerman sent him onto the field in the 63rd minute, Messi received the ball, Vilmos Vanczak grabbed his shirt, and the Argentine responded by trying to break free with his arm. The referee interpreted it as aggression. Red card. 47 seconds had passed . FIFA still remembers that episode as one of the strangest international beginnings of a superstar.

The first great joy would come in Beijing 2008 . In a squad of enormous stature that included Sergio Agüero, Ángel Di María, Javier Mascherano and Juan Román Riquelme, Messi won the Olympic gold medal. There was still a long way to go before carrying those triumphs with the youth teams over to the senior national team, where his relationship with Argentina would go through a much more painful period.

Brazil 2014: the World Cup that almost changed everything

The 2014 World Cup in Brazil was Messi's first great opportunity to touch glory with the senior national team.

He scored four goals in the group stage, including the dramatic strike against Iran and a brace against Nigeria, and in the round of 16 he assisted Ángel Di María for the goal that eliminated Switzerland . Argentina advanced to the final after getting past Belgium and the Netherlands, while Messi established himself as the offensive محور of a team that was returning to a World Cup final after 24 years.

At the Maracanã, Argentina fell 1-0 to Germany due to Mario Götze's goal in extra time, after having had several chances to take the lead.

Messi finished the tournament with four goals, one assist, and the Golden Ball for the best player of the World Cup, but the image that remained was another one: walking just a few centimeters from the Cup before receiving his award.

The blow was even greater two years later. Argentina lost again to Chile in the final of the 2016 Copa América Centenario, Messi missed his penalty in the shootout and, completely devastated, uttered a phrase that seemed to bring the story to a close:

“It’s over for me with the national team”. It was his fourth lost final with Argentina.

But that goodbye barely lasted 66 days. After a conversation in Barcelona with Edgardo Bauza, the new Argentina coach, Messi returned against Uruguay, scored the winning goal and once again took the lead of the Albiceleste. The wildest display would come in October 2017: Argentina were on the ropes in the qualifiers for Russia 2018, they started by losing to Ecuador in Quito and Messi responded with a hat-trick that took the team to the World Cup.

Maracanã: the night when everything changed

It was necessary to wait until July 10, 2021 for one of the heaviest burdens of his career to finally disappear. Argentina defeated Brazil 1-0 at the Maracanã with a goal by Ángel Di María and Messi won his first major title with the senior national team.

The image was different from all the previous ones. This time Messi did not walk alongside someone else’s Cup nor end up sitting alone after a defeat. He fell to his knees on the grass and, within seconds, all his teammates ran toward him. After years of hearing that with Argentina he could not repeat what he had achieved in Barcelona, he had torn down the barrier that seemed impossible. Not only did he manage to embrace his teammates, but he created an unbreakable bond with the entire Argentine people . That triumph ended 28 years without titles for the senior national team and opened the most successful stage of Messi’s career wearing the Argentina shirt.

A year later came the Finalissima against Italy at Wembley. Argentina won 3-0 and confirmed that that Copa América had not been an isolated episode. Lionel Scaloni's team had found an identity, and Messi, surrounded by a generation that had grown up admiring him, seemed to finally play freed from the burden he had carried for much of his career.

Qatar: the kiss that changed the whole story

And then Qatar 2022 arrived.

Argentina started by losing unexpectedly to Saudi Arabia and once again found itself staring into the abyss.

In the next group-stage match , Messi scored against Mexico, the team reacted and began a run that ended up becoming one of the most extraordinary stories in World Cup history.

Messi scored in the round of 16 against Australia, in the quarterfinals against the Netherlands, in the semifinals against Croatia, and twice against France in the final.

Argentina survived the 3-3 draw and won on penalties in what is considered one of the best finals in World Cup history.

At 35 years old, in his fifth World Cup, the captain finally lifted the trophy he had pursued throughout his entire life . He finished with seven goals and was named the tournament’s best player.

The photograph of Messi kissing the World Cup was much more than just another celebration . It abruptly put an end to all those debates about his relationship with Argentina: the Maracanã in 2014, the finals against Chile, the 2016 retirement, and the years in which every defeat became a judgment on his figure.

At the 2024 Copa América, Argentina were crowned champions once again after defeating Colombia in Miami. Messi had to leave that final injured and in tears, a gesture that was among the most amateurish in football but that showed how deeply the sport reached his very core.

Lautaro Martínez appeared in extra time to give the captain another continental title.

The last World Cup still had one more madness in store

At 39 years old, Messi decided to play in the 2026 World Cup and once again defied all logic.

He scored eight goals, won the Silver Boot, and led Argentina to another final. In the semifinals he did not score against England, but he provided both assists in the 2-1 comeback: Enzo Fernández equalized in the 85th minute and Lautaro Martínez scored the qualifying goal in the 90+2.

Spain prevented the perfect ending. Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute of extra time and La Roja defeated Argentina 1-0 in New Jersey. Messi ended his sixth World Cup with 21 goals in 34 World Cup matches and another final played. Weeks later, he announced his international retirement.

But one scene was still missing.

It couldn’t end in New Jersey. He couldn’t do it far from home. That’s why Argentina and the AFA organized this final match against Benin at the Monumental under a phrase that sums up better than any statistic what will happen this Tuesday: “The night no one wants to end.”

More than two decades after that long-haired boy who walked off in tears after receiving a red card 47 seconds into his debut, Messi will once again walk onto a field wearing the Argentina shirt. This time there will be no other World Cup to chase, no other revenge to await, nor another final left unfinished.

All that will remain is to say goodbye and keep enjoying the greatest footballer of all time.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo explains his departure from Portugal: "Believe me, this is the pure truth"
articles.standfirst: The Portuguese striker points at Jorge Jesus and accuses him of lying
articles.summary: The Portuguese striker points at Jorge Jesus and accuses him of lying
articles.body:
C ristiano Ronaldo has given his explanations, as he promised after leaving Portugal's training camp.

Cristiano Ronaldo's Statement

As I promised, I decided to recount, in the first person and directly, the circumstances that surrounded the final stage of the National Team's journey.

After the 2026 World Cup, I prepared a letter to the Portuguese people, which I still keep, with the words I want to address to them when I definitively leave our team.

At the end of the competition, on the return flight from the United States, the President of the Federation asked me and insisted that I reconsider my decision to leave because the FPF wanted me to continue.

Immediately afterwards, he asked for my opinion on the name of the current National Team Coach, whom he was considering, along with other names he did not reveal to me.

I replied to the President of the Federation that, in my opinion, it would be the right choice. Therefore, on the day the current National Team Coach was introduced, I felt truly happy with the choice. It was the right option, as the results show.

A few days later, I received an initial contact from the new national team coach saying that he would like to meet with me in person. I replied yes, and we scheduled it for the end of my vacation.

We met at Football City, where my club was holding its preseason training camp.

That day, the coach told me that he was counting on me and that my presence was essential to his project. He presented me with a plan for my participation right then and there. He told me that I would play the first and the last match and that, for physical preparation reasons, he would always make three or four changes per match.

At that moment, he suggested that I not travel with the national team to Norway and Denmark. He proposed that I play the first match and stay in Portugal, then rejoin before the match at the Dragão stadium.

I immediately rejected the proposal. It seemed obvious to me that I couldn't accept it. Not playing the matches abroad didn't mean I wouldn't be the team captain. That privilege of staying in Portugal would not be a good example.

Finally, the coach agreed with my analysis.

Simão Coutinho, Al Nassr's sporting director, attended this conversation, the person to whom the current national team coach reported throughout last season and one of those responsible for his signing by the club in 2025.

On the eve of the training camp, the head coach came to my house in Lisbon to speak with me again, at his own request. The conversation was calm and all the principles agreed upon in August were maintained. I played the match at Alvalade, and although I was substituted, I did not cause any problems. I personally put the captain's armband on Bruno Fernandes, far from imagining that I might be taking my last steps as an athlete and captain of the national team. The important thing that day, for me, was our victory. Winning is always good; in Portugal and for my country, even better.

At lunchtime on the day of the match in Norway, an assistant to the national team coach came over to the table where the group was having lunch and informed me that the coach wanted to speak with me. To my absolute surprise, the coach asked me if I was okay to play 30 minutes. I was completely focused on my physical recovery, integrated with my teammates as always, and thinking that I would not play that day. There was no problem.

This request was outside my recovery and physical training plan, since I was only going to play on the 4th at the Dragão stadium, but obviously I said yes. He replied that I had to be prepared because I would play 30 minutes.

The rest is history. I warmed up from halftime, watched the minutes go by, and they didn't call me. The coach had broken his word.

At the end of the match, I just wanted everything to end with a victory and to be alone. I didn’t go over to greet the fans. A mistake that is solely my responsibility and that should never have happened. I apologize to the Portuguese people who supported us intensely there, I apologize to the fans, and I apologize to those who, without being Portuguese, traveled there to see me and whom I may have disappointed.

Forty-eight hours later, we had a conversation: me, the coach and Simão Coutinho, since he had been following our conversations in August.

It was a profound and very frank moment, without filters.

We agreed that there was only one way to close this "case": that the coach would repeat what he had just told me in private, in the presence of Simão Coutinho, but in the press room.

The agreement was simple: the coach would begin the press conference with this topic, trying to put the matter to rest by telling the truth. He would say that I never asked to play any minutes, that it was the coach, and no one else, who proposed the plan for this training camp, and that it was a mistake to make me warm up only not to play, and that if it happened again, I would not do it.

We ended that meeting with the coach asking me for a hug, promising me that he would say at the press conference what he had just told me, and that the matter was resolved. I would not play in Denmark, but I would in the match against Dragão. All of this took place in the presence of Simão Coutinho, as always.

At the coach's request, a videoconference was held between him, Simão Coutinho and Tiago Craveiro, in which what we had discussed was summarized.

A brief document was prepared, which I personally reviewed and which, to my knowledge, was delivered to the coach, just as he had requested.

'The conference unfolded as expected: his attitude had nothing to do with our meeting; I perceived expressions and aggression that I consider undeserved, an attitude of "I want, I can, and I command" that he had never shown me before, not even remotely, in private, the day before.'

The notes I validated were the following: "I think it is important, because it is the truth, to clarify some things before talking about Denmark:'

1. I personally proposed a plan for Cristiano, with no one else involved, for him this season with the National Team. It was a long and very good conversation.

2. I know how much he lives for and loves the National Team and the weight it carries in the world; moreover, the weight and positive influence he has had on the National Team for 24 consecutive years.

3. The plan I proposed to Cristiano was accepted.

4. He never questioned my decisions. He was exemplary, loyal, and professional.

5. The match against Norway was not included in the plan I had outlined for him. However, I felt that he had managed to recover physically from the first match and I warned him that I might have to use him. Cristiano agreed.

6. I made a mistake by making someone of Pelé or Maradona's stature warm up only to not put him in the match. If it were today, I wouldn't do it.

7. To conclude: I want Cristiano in the National Team. "Actually, I don't want a little, I want a lot. Luckily, he believes in me too. He believed in Al Nassr and here as well."

8. Regarding not greeting the fans. We've already talked about that. Someone who has played more than 230 matches for the National Team doesn't get lessons in love for Portugal from me. It was a moment of frustration that doesn't erase anything. He is the player who signs the most autographs, takes the most selfies, and shows the most affection to the fans. Let's not invent problems where there are none. When we're not happy, we react. That's all.

None of those reports, therefore, said that the coach had apologized to me.

It was the second time I had broken my word.

I decided to leave the training camp without waiting for another broken promise. For me, the truth remains the most important thing in interpersonal relationships. No matter how much it hurts, I want people to tell me the truth.

In fact, in a conversation I had with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation and the coach on the morning of that press conference, which they can surely confirm, I reiterated that if they did not want me there, they simply had to tell me. They only needed to be honest with me. I would accept it and I promised that we would prepare something beautiful, as I dream will happen, and no one would get upset.

"I remember it as if it were yesterday. They answered in unison that no. That my place was in the National Team.

Never, at no time, have I interfered in any technical or tactical decision of any coach or national team manager in almost 25 years of my career. I accept, for better or worse, what they propose to do. I respect the decision, and when they break their word to me, I feel that my place is not there.

I also owe an apology to my teammates on the national team for leaving the training camp. Despite the absolute lack of trust in the coach's word, as anyone who witnessed those conversations can attest, I should not have done it. The responsibility is exclusively mine.

I apologize once again to the Portuguese people, but breaking my word has a decisive impact on me. I felt that, from that moment on, my staying would only harm the team, and I did what I always said I would do if I didn’t feel useful: I packed my bags and left.

The consequences of my actions must be evaluated and sanctioned by the Portuguese Football Federation. I believe the punishment should not be reduced. I am not just any player; I am the team captain, and that is an aggravating factor. I have already apologized, but I know that actions must have consequences. Anyone in football, like me, knows that, regardless of individual position, the rules are the same for everyone.

Believe me, this is the plain truth.

Cristiano Ronaldo's Statement
As I promised, I decided to recount, in the first person and directly, the circumstances that surrounded the final stage of the National Team's journey.
After the 2026 World Cup, I prepared a letter to the Portuguese people, which I still keep, with the words I want to address to them when I definitively leave our team.

Immediately afterwards, he asked for my opinion on the name of the current National Team Coach, whom he was considering, along with other names he did not reveal to me.

I replied to the President of the Federation that, in my opinion, it would be the right choice. Therefore, on the day the current National Team Coach was introduced, I felt truly happy with the choice. It was the right option, as the results show.

We met at Football City, where my club was holding its preseason training camp.

I immediately rejected the proposal. It seemed obvious to me that I couldn't accept it. Not playing the matches abroad didn't mean I wouldn't be the team captain. That privilege of staying in Portugal would not be a good example.

Simão Coutinho, Al Nassr's sporting director, attended this conversation, the person to whom the current national team coach reported throughout last season and one of those responsible for his signing by the club in 2025.

articles.title: The stars bid farewell to Messi: "The best in history, extraterrestrial"
articles.standfirst: Ronaldinho, Neymar, Modric, and other players praise Leo in his farewell to the national team
articles.summary: Ronaldinho, Neymar, Modric, and other players praise Leo in his farewell to the national team
articles.body:
Messi put an end to his spell with the national team . He leaves behind titles, goals and memorable performances, and ahead of him he creates a void that will be difficult to fill in the Albiceleste . As soon as the match against Benin ended, his last with his national side, praise for him followed. Leo received beautiful words from both teammates and rivals.

' Ronaldinho left one of the most emotional messages. "What a pleasure and what joy to have been part of your story from day one, brother! You made us smile and enjoy football so much... Your name is in the history of your country, and of the whole world. Only we know the joy we felt in fulfilling our childhood dream, representing our entire nation and becoming world champions. You gave everything for your national team and for your country. I understand you perfectly and I know that everything related to family makes us rethink things. Enjoy life, brother. I wish you the best, today and always," he wrote on "X".'

I understand you perfectly, and I know that everything related to family makes us rethink things. Enjoy life, brother

Neymar also joined the public tribute. "Anyone who loves football has enjoyed you over these years… Today is your last match wearing your national team's jersey, your country's jersey, and I hope you enjoy every second, that all of today's tributes make you happy. It's not only Argentina that thanks you, the world thanks you for everything you did for football. Thank you for making me love football even more; it was an honor to have played against you and even more so to make history by your side. Thank you, Leo Messi," he posted on his social media.

Whoever loves football enjoyed you throughout these years

' Modric referred to Leo's farewell after Croatia's match against Spain. "What can you say about Messi? It's a shame that he is saying goodbye to his national team, but it's his decision and it has to be respected. He won the World Cup he wanted, he is one of the best players in the world and it has been a pleasure to watch him play, although I have suffered a lot because of him with the national team and with Madrid. He is a unique footballer. I wish him the best of luck," he said.'

It has been a pleasure to watch him play, although I have suffered a lot because of him with the national team and with Madrid. He is a unique footballer.

' Arturo Vidal , although more brief, paid tribute to Messi on Instagram. "Today you play your last match for your country, my friend. I wish you the very best always. The best in history, extraterrestrial".'

I wish you all the best always. The best in history, extraterrestrial

For me, you will always be the greatest

One of the most emotional messages from his current national team teammates was from Julián Alvarez . "What a privilege it was to share the field and so many moments with you. First, I admired you as a kid, like millions of Argentines who grew up dreaming of becoming footballers because of you. Then, I was lucky enough to meet you, be your teammate, and experience things I will never forget. Thank you for everything you gave us, for representing our country the way you did, and for leaving us a legacy that goes far beyond football. We’re going to miss you so much in the sky blue and white. To me, you will always be the greatest. Thank you so much, Leo," he posted on Instagram.

articles.title: Messi, Right-Footed for a Night: The Unusual Drone Glitch During His Farewell
articles.standfirst: The tribute following the 3-0 win over Benin produced an unexpected image: the drones depicted Messi striking the ball with his right foot, and drew boos when they first displayed a sponsor’s logo
articles.summary: The tribute following the 3-0 win over Benin produced an unexpected image: the drones depicted Messi striking the ball with his right foot, and drew boos when they first displayed a sponsor’s logo
articles.body:
Lionel Messi’s farewell from the Argentine national team featured tears, a goal, two assists, and a Monumental Stadium paying tribute to its captain. It also included a curious mistake that quickly went viral: the drones participating in the tribute depicted the No. 10 striking the ball with his right foot.

The spectacle took place after the 3-0 victory over Benin , in Messi’s final match with the Albiceleste in front of an Argentine home crowd. As the captain and his teammates remained on the field, hundreds of lights began to form various images from his career in the sky.

Among them was the silhouette of Messi standing in front of a soccer ball. Everything seemed to fit until fans noticed a detail that was hard to miss: the drone-rendered Messi was right-footed . The Argentine, one of the most recognizable left-footed players in soccer history, was shown shooting with his non-dominant foot. The mistake quickly spread across social media, where comments such as “Chiqui Tapia did it” and “WHAT A BLUNDER” began to appear.

Messi, with the Wrong Foot

Messi has scored goals with both feet, but his career is closely tied to his left foot. With it, he has built a large part of his repertoire: ball control, dribbling, feints, assists, and the vast majority of his goals.

That’s why the image drew so much attention on a night designed precisely to look back on his career. The tribute sought to revisit some of the most iconic moments of his career and ended up featuring an unexpected scene as well.

That wasn't the only detail that sparked comments during the show. Before the tribute to Messi began, drones displayed the logo and name of an insurance company that was sponsoring the game . The commercial appearance drew boos from the stands and criticism from fans, who had expected the show to begin immediately with images of the captain.

Then came the tribute dedicated to number 10. The drones formed the AFA crest with its three stars, a jersey bearing the surname “Messi” and the number 10, and various images related to his titles and his career with Argentina.

The World Cup trophy won in Qatar also appeared, and toward the end, the message “Thank you, Leo!” accompanied by the three stars. The final image was Messi’s face in profile against the backdrop of the Monumental. The AFA confirmed that the drone show was part of the display prepared for the farewell, along with the lights, fireworks, and musical performances.

This isn't the first time Messi has accidentally used his right foot

The drone blooper had a recent precedent. In early September, LEGO also depicted Messi kicking with his right foot in an animation released as a tribute to the Argentine after he announced his retirement from the national team.

In the video, a minifigure wearing the number 10 walks through a stadium tunnel, steps onto the field, and finds a ball. The final scene shows little Messi shooting with his right foot. The brand accompanied the post with the message: “The boy who entered the tunnel became the legend who changed the game. Thanks for everything, Leo!”

This detail didn’t go unnoticed back then either. Fans immediately noticed that the figure was using the wrong leg and turned the tribute into yet another little anecdote about Messi’s left foot. LEGO also offers official products inspired by the soccer player.

This time, it was the drones that repeated the mistak e. On a night that will be remembered for Messi’s emotion, his final goal with Argentina, and a farewell in front of more than 85,000 people , the right-footed version of No. 10 ended up earning its own place among the night’s memorable images.

articles.title: Woman tears up boyfriend’s ticket to Messi’s farewell after spotting a message on his phone
articles.standfirst: A fan experienced a true nightmare at the entrances to the Monumental Stadium after being left out of Messi's last match with the Argentina national team following an altercation with his ex-partner
articles.summary: A fan experienced a true nightmare at the entrances to the Monumental Stadium after being left out of Messi's last match with the Argentina national team following an altercation with his ex-partner
articles.body:
'The clash of the Albiceleste against Benin at River Plate's stadium was packed with emotion from start to finish , with massive celebrations, top-level musical performances, and a packed stadium that bid the Rosario star farewell through tears after a 3-0 win . However, the unforgettable night in Buenos Aires had an unusual flip side in the surroundings of the sports venue.'

While thousands of fans celebrated the Albiceleste victory and the emotional tribute to the star, one supporter became the night's biggest loser . Amid the security checks, the man broke down in tears when he realized he would not be able to enter the stands after an issue with his ticket .

The unusual incident gained national attention when the affected man recounted his ordeal to the microphones of the media covering the pre-match buildup . According to what he said in a television interview given to the streaming channel AZZ, after a heated argument at the entrance gates, his ex-girlfriend tore up his paper tickets .

From love to tears at the Núñez entrances

"First, Messi, we love you. Second, I’m having the worst night of my life: my ex just tore up my ticket. She’s inside and I can’t get in" , he said heartbroken in front of the cameras in the area around Monumental Stadium.

The fan's pain multiplied as he detailed the enormous financial impact of the incident. The supporter revealed that he had paid 800,000 Argentine pesos for a pair of tickets bought at the last minute on the informal resale market to secure his presence at the Núñez venue.

"I just bought them on resale, I paid 800 grand, 400 grand each. I spoke with the head of security and he threw me out. I went to the Lower Centenario, they scanned it and told me it was invalid" , the fan explained indignantly over the frustrating situation.

Controversy and suspicions on social media

The heartbreaking testimony spread very quickly on digital platforms such as X, where various users and local media outlets such as the portal Contexto Tucumán and Infobae amplified the images of the fan with the ticket torn to pieces .

Various theories immediately emerged among internet users: while some showed empathy for the victim in the face of the unusual scene of spite, others speculated that it was a desperate ploy to convince security after having been scammed with fake resale tickets .

The scandal of the destroyed ticket contrasted with the enormous demand and the widespread frenzy caused by the Flea's farewell in the Argentine capital . With a stadium packed with more than 80,000 spectators, official tickets sold out in a matter of minutes, causing prices on the black market to skyrocket to astronomical figures.

Messi's tears and the emotion of the celebration

For those who managed to get past the turnstiles, the night at the Monumental offered an unforgettable spectacle marked by football and music . With goals from Nicolás Otamendi, Nico Paz, and Lionel Messi himself from the penalty spot, the Argentina National Team defeated Benin 3-0 in a match that served as the perfect setting for the big celebration afterward .

The culminating moment of the post-match celebrations came with the emotional musical segment prepared to pay tribute to the legend from Rosario. According to the outlet TN Show, one of the most moving moments occurred when singer Soledad Pastorutti took the stage to perform “Brindis” , the iconic song that years earlier she had also dedicated to Diego Armando Maradona .

The emotional performance brought Lionel Messi himself to tears , as he could not contain his emotion alongside his wife Antonela Roccuzzo and his children Thiago, Mateo, and Ciro right there on the pitch. At the end of the song, the artist from Santa Fe and the Argentine captain shared an emotional embrace that was applauded by the entire stadium .

The festive atmosphere that brought together prominent musical artists in Núñez left an unforgettable image in the history of world football. However , for the unfortunate fan who was left at the outer gates with a torn ticket and empty pockets , the historic tribute evening will be remembered forever as the bitterest moment of his life .

articles.title: Messi has a distasteful moment as players fail to read the room during Argentina farewell
articles.standfirst: A moment that briefly took away from what was supposed to be an emotional night for the Argentina captain
articles.summary: A moment that briefly took away from what was supposed to be an emotional night for the Argentina captain
articles.body:
For Argentinians and soccer fans around the world, it was time to say goodbye to a legend. Lionel Messi decided it was time to take a step back from the national team , closing another chapter with the country he has represented for so many years. Messi is an idol both on and off the pitch, not only for Argentinians but for millions of fans around the world.

Even fellow players still look up to Messi

That admiration also exists within soccer itself, with players often looking up to legends of the game . That was the case for the Benin players, who were Argentina's opponents in Messi's final game. It was surely a moment the African team will never forget, but one interaction with Messi became an uncomfortable part of the night as the captain tried to absorb every second of his final day with Argentina.

One Benin player was clearly excited about the moment and the opportunity to be around Messi, but he failed to read the room despite Messi's attempts to move on. The African player tried twice to take a selfie with the Argentine star , while Messi simply wanted to soak in the moment with his country, his team and his family. Cameras captured Messi moving him away on both occasions as he tried to stay in the moment.

Messi's reaction may have looked rude, but the timing mattered

The Argentina captain's gesture understandably came across as rude , but it was also difficult to see the Benin player continue trying after it was clear Messi was not looking for a photo . It may have been the player's only opportunity to take a selfie with one of his idols, but this was Messi's final home game with Argentina, and he wanted to live every remaining minute of it.

The country came to a standstill after Messi's farewell, while those who had the privilege of attending the home game spent the night praising and applauding him. Fortunately , the moment with the Benin players did not completely overshadow what was otherwise an emotional night for Messi and Argentina.

articles.summary: The footage shows a side of the Argentine rarely seen by fans
articles.body:
N eymar is once again at the center of controversy after sharing a video capturing a private moment between himself, Lionel Messi and Luis Suárez. The footage stands out because it shows the Argentine in a way fans rarely, if ever, get to see him.

Many believe the Brazilian showed poor judgment by making the video public. It features the three players drunk and dancing during Barcelona's celebrations after winning the Champions League in 2015. Neymar revisited the moment in his Netflix documentary, Neymar: The Perfect Chaos , while going through videos saved on his phone.

Messi rarely finds himself in this kind of controversy

Not everyone was happy to see such a private moment shared publicly, particularly because Messi is rarely involved in scandals surrounding parties or inappropriate behavior . Some argued that if the footage had emerged at the time, the three players would have faced heavy criticism, while Barcelona's reputation could also have taken a hit because of their condition during the celebration.

Fans question the reaction to the footage

However, some fans considered the public reaction an overreaction, arguing that the video simply showed players celebrating a major achievement. From their perspective, the three had just had too much to drink, something that could happen to anyone, and were not doing anything wrong.

Still, for those who criticized the post, the main issue was not necessarily what Messi, Neymar and Suárez were doing in the video, but t he fact that Neymar chose to share such a private moment with the public.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Messi playing together on the same team?
articles.standfirst: Carlos Tévez is working to organize a match at La Bombonera at the end of the year
articles.summary: Carlos Tévez is working to organize a match at La Bombonera at the end of the year
articles.body:
One of football's "unfinished business" is to see Cristiano Ronaldo and Messi sharing a team . The two most important figures in the sport in the 21st Century and practically in the entire history of this sport are in the final years of their careers after two decades of shining... and now one person wants to bring them together to "close the circle".

That person is Carlos Tévez, a former Argentine footballer who retired in 2022 and who was left with the lingering regret of not having had a farewell match at La Bombonera. Now, "El Apache" seems to have revived the idea of organizing it at the end of 2026 and, according to Infobae, already has the approval of Juan Román Riquelme to do it. And at that event, which would be on December 20, Messi and Cristiano would be there... playing for the same team.

I’m going to go get Cristiano myself

A few weeks ago, the former footballer already said on the Argentine streaming channel "OLGA" that he was preparing the event and gave some details. "It would be very nice, I have to talk to Román to do it at the end of the year ," he began by saying before revealing some of the names who would be there and with whom he has shared a team.

"Goalkeepers, Buffon and Van der Sar ; defenders Ferdinand, Vidic, Chiellini, Bonucci; midfielders Pirlo, Scholes, Riquelme ...", he explained to the panelists, who described it as "the best friendly match in history" before referring to the issue of Cristiano and Messi. " We're bringing them together" , Tévez said emphatically. " I'll go get Cristiano myself, and the little guy -referring to Messi- too" , he added.

Carlos Tévez played 47 matches with Messi for the Argentina national team and a total of 80 matches with Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United. Now he wants to bring them together to achieve a unique image that could last for eternity.

articles.body:
P ies Morgan , Cristiano Ronaldo 's cinfidant in the english press revealed the message CR7 sent him about a pundit .

Simon Jordan is a businessman (he made his initial fortune in the prepaid mobile phone sector with the company Pocket Phone Shop), columnist, journalist (co-host of the daily sports program White and Jordan) and popular British sports media commentator.

articles.title: Messi chose the 10 future stars of football: Arsenal, Chelsea and Boca Juniors have representatives
articles.standfirst: The Argentine stars in the third season of “Messi +10,” Adidas’s campaign that brings together ten footballers from different countries. Argentine player Tomas Aranda and Mexican Gilberto Mora appear among the most prominent names.
articles.summary: The Argentine stars in the third season of “Messi +10,” Adidas’s campaign that brings together ten footballers from different countries. Argentine player Tomas Aranda and Mexican Gilberto Mora appear among the most prominent names.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi once again named the footballers he considers part of the next generation. The Argentine took part in the third edition of “Messi +10” , Adidas’s initiative that brings together ten young talents from men’s and women’s football under one team.

The list includes familiar names, but also less predictable picks. Max Dowman, from Arsenal, and Chloe Sarwie, from Chelsea, appear among the ten selected, while the roster is not limited to Europe’s major academies and leaves out several of the young players currently drawing the most media attention.

Messi backed two young players from Arsenal and Chelsea

One of the names that draws the most attention is Max Dowman, one of Arsenal's greatest prospects. At just 16 years old, the forward has already featured for the first team and has become one of the most closely watched talents in the Gunners' academy.

The other English representative is Chloe Sarwie, a Chelsea footballer. The 17-year-old has also taken her first steps with the first team and has been gaining prominence in England’s youth ranks.

The selection of both is especially striking because Messi did not build a list solely around the most established names among the new figures of European football. Instead, the campaign included players with very different career paths and levels of exposure.

Tomás Aranda, the only Argentine chosen by Messi

The list also has a particularity for Argentine soccer: Tomás Aranda, from Boca Juniors , is Messi’s only compatriot among the ten selected. The 19-year-old attacking midfielder is going through his first season with greater continuity in senior soccer and already has 14 appearances for the Xeneize side.

Aranda also recently had contact with the Argentina national team, a detail that helps explain why his name is starting to gain traction among the young players to watch. His inclusion gives Boca a direct presence on a list that combines prospects from Europe and the Americas and that, in this edition, reserves only one spot for an Argentine footballer.

The 10 names chosen by Messi

Among the selected are also Zavier Gozo , an American player linked to Crystal Palace; Tomás Aranda , from Boca Juniors; Gilberto Mora , from Tijuana and one of the major recent breakout talents in Mexican soccer; and Can Uzun , a forward for Eintracht Frankfurt and the Turkish national team.

The list is completed by Kees Smit, from AZ Alkmaar; Jesús Rodríguez, from Como; Lotta Wrede, from Hamburger SV; and Giovanna Waksman, a footballer for Lyon. The selection mixes players from Europe and America and maintains the formula of including talents from men's and women's football.

Messi had already chosen another Premier League gem

This is not the first time that one of Messi's choices in this campaign has drawn attention. In the previous edition, Rio Ngumoha had appeared, one of Liverpool's great prospects, along with players such as Andrey Santos and Kendry Páez.

Adidas unveiled this third generation under the slogan “The next chapter begins here” , with Messi as the central figure of the campaign. More than an official ranking, it is a promotional selection of emerging talents, but the Argentine’s presence turns every name into a choice that quickly comes under scrutiny.

articles.summary: FIFA rented for nearly 4 million dollars for more than seven years an office that remained almost empty in the towers of the president of the United States
articles.body:
Today, Le Monde reveals one of the links between United States President Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino , president of FIFA, but going far beyond their friendship forged during the organization of the last World Cup or the Peace Prize that world football’s top governing body awarded to Trump himself. The French newspaper claims it has obtained documents proving that FIFA rented offices in Trump Tower that were empty for seven years for 4 million dollars.

"How much is the rent that the International Football Federation (FIFA) pays to the Trump clan, since the body set up an office on June 1, 2025 on the 17th floor of Trump Tower in New York? According to internal documents accessed by Le Monde, the global organization has agreed to pay a total of nearly 4 million dollars (3.57 million dollars) over seven years and seven months for the 450-square-meter premises, which remains for the most part unoccupied. The agreement highlights the close ties between FIFA president Gianni Infantino and the occupant of the White House, Donald Trump," Le Monde notes.

'FIFA, through its subsidiary FIFA Americas Incorporation, legally based in the state of Delaware, agreed to pay that amount to the New York-based company starting in June 2025 Trump Tower Commercial LLC, chaired by Eric Trump, son of Donald Trump, owner and manager of the building. "The contract was signed by four members of the board of directors in May 2025, with the signature of its secretary general, Mattias Grafström, on the first line," the French newspaper adds. '

According to these documents, FIFA did not visit other locations or compare offers with other companies before choosing Trump Tower as its headquarters. Contrary to what it had done in Miami. In light of these facts, several members of FIFA's administration internally expressed concern about the office lease, pointing to a possible conflict of interest and the fact that the process had not followed the usual procedure.

FIFA pays, on average, the private company linked to the U.S. president around $470,000 a year—or $41,000 a month—for 1701, according to calculations by the French outlet. In other words, market rates for offices of this size on New York’s Fifth Avenue. The lease contract includes "a fixed annual 2% increase [in rent] as a transfer of operating expenses." Although at the start of the contract a clause resembling a discount was included—fixed rent will be reduced by $19,000 per month during each of the first eight full months following the effective date—the amount is higher at the end of the contract: $533,000 for the last seven months, compared with $455,000 in the second year. "FIFA pays market-rate rent for these premises and complies with all local legislation," the international organization explained in response to Le Monde’s inquiry.

articles.title: Jorge Jesus' lawyer takes a swipe at Cristiano Ronaldo: "The gods end up alone on Olympus surrounded by mirrors"
articles.standfirst: He said goodbye to his column in the Portuguese newspaper Record, a daily in which CR7 is a shareholder
articles.summary: He said goodbye to his column in the Portuguese newspaper Record, a daily in which CR7 is a shareholder
articles.body:
A new episode in the conflict between Cristiano Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus in the Portugal national team. Luis Henrique , the Portuguese coach's lawyer, has written a scathing column against the Portuguese star titled "My last dance" , in which he announces that it will be his last column in the Récord newspaper due to the media outlet's ties to the Al Nassr footballer.

"There are columns that are written with the heart and others with the conscience. This one belongs to the latter, and will most likely be the last one I sign here. Not because of anyone's imposition, but because of a purely and simply personal decision . For me, the facts are very simple: Cristiano Ronaldo is a leading shareholder of Medialivre, owner of this newspaper", he recalled.

' "Given that the captain maintains an open conflict with Jorge Jesús and, by extension, with myself, it would not be appropriate—indeed, it would be shameful—for me to continue collaborating with and receiving remuneration from a company in which he is a shareholder. There is no intellectual independence without financial independence. Whoever expresses opinions about power cannot depend on the power they express opinions about. It is from this tie that I prefer to free myself from this very moment , so that no one, whoever they may be, thinks or dreams of having the ability to impose any ‘consequence’ on me," he stated.'

“Freedom that is only exercised when it costs nothing is called convenience. And I have never written for convenience ,” he recalled.

Harsh message to Cristiano Ronaldo

Jorge Jesus's lawyer ended his column by addressing the Portuguese star directly. “ Lastly, a few words for Cristiano Ronaldo. A large part of what you have achieved for yourself, for your family and for your country has been defended and praised here, and reminded to those who had most forgotten it,” he stated.

"However, through your actions, your behavior, and your obsession with certain indicators, you achieve something that no opponent ever managed: to spoil our ability to remember all the good you have brought us. You surround yourself more and more with those who tell you what you want to hear and less and less with those who tell you what you need to hear," he warned.

'"That is the fate of gods and autocrats: they end up alone on Olympus, surrounded by mirrors ," he declared.'

articles.title: Rooney hits out at Cristiano: "He is not handling the end of his international career well"
articles.standfirst: The former striker and teammate of the Portuguese at Manchester United acknowledges that he believes he is not handling well the moment of saying goodbye to football
articles.summary: The former striker and teammate of the Portuguese at Manchester United acknowledges that he believes he is not handling well the moment of saying goodbye to football
articles.body:
The repercussions of Cristiano Ronaldo's dazzling departure from the Portugal national team's training camp during this past international break are still being felt. The latest to speak about what the Portuguese star did has been his former Manchester United teammate , Wayne Rooney, who once again criticized Cristiano's attitude.

' "The first thing I said to myself was "why?" Undermining your coach, your teammates in the way he did was very wrong," began the former Red Devil striker on the Stick to United program, who insisted that everything that happened from a footballing point of view was wrong. '

Rooney criticized the striker for trying to publicly influence his national team coach's remarks after the incident. " You can't tell a coach what he has to say . That goes beyond anything I've ever seen," the Englishman said.

It's uncomfortable to watch

"The harshest reflection came when addressing Cristiano's current situation with the Portuguese national team. For Rooney, the problem goes beyond a simple falling-out with the coach.

"All players reach the moment to leave international football. It comes to everyone and, unfortunately, he is not handling it well . It is uncomfortable to watch," he stated.

articles.title: The reason Piers Morgan considers Cristiano Ronaldo to be the greatest of all time, ahead of Messi
articles.standfirst: The British broadcaster points to Ronaldo's incredible records while making controversial claim about Messi's place in Argentine football history
articles.summary: The British broadcaster points to Ronaldo's incredible records while making controversial claim about Messi's place in Argentine football history
articles.body:
The debate over soccer 's greatest player has followed Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi throughout their careers, but Piers Morgan believes one crucial distinction should settle the argument in the Portuguese forward's favor.

The outspoken British broadcaster argues that Ronaldo 's willingness to compete in different countries, combined with his extraordinary goalscoring achievements, gives him an advantage over his longtime rival.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Morgan defended his preference for the former Manchester United and Real Madrid forward while acknowledging that supporters of Messi are entitled to reach a different conclusion.

"Ronaldo, I think, has tested himself and challenged himself a lot more than Messi did," Morgan said. "He has scored a lot more goals and broken many records that Messi does not hold."

Why Morgan believes Ronaldo has edge over Messi

Morgan 's argument centers on Ronaldo 's ability to maintain his goalscoring standards while adapting to different leagues and playing environments throughout his career.

The Portuguese international has won domestic championships in England, Spain, Italy and Saudi Arabia, having represented Manchester United, Real Madrid, Juventus and Al-Nassr .

"But look, the beauty of football, it is all subjective. If other people prefer Messi, good luck to you," Morgan said during the interview.

"But the advantage Ronaldo has is statistics. Nobody has won the league in more countries than him, nobody has scored more goals than he has, and no one has scored more international goals than he has."

Ronaldo recently scored his 981st career goal during Al-Nassr 's 3-1 victory over Neftchi , moving closer to becoming the first player to reach 1,000 official senior goals.

His international record is equally significant, with 146 goals for Portugal strengthening his claim as one of the most prolific players soccer has produced.

Messi , meanwhile, has scored 934 career goals according to the figures cited in the discussion, despite making 161 fewer appearances than Ronaldo.

Morgan ranks Diego Maradona above Lionel Messi

Morgan 's comments became particularly provocative when he questioned whether Messi should even be regarded as Argentina's greatest soccer player.

"Messi is a great player, he is one of the greatest players of all time. But, I don't think he is even the best Argentinian," Morgan said.

"I think Maradona was the greatest Argentinian football player and I will put him above Messi."

The assessment is likely to divide supporters given Messi 's eight Ballon d'Or awards, his achievements with Barcelona and his leadership of Argentina's victorious 2022 World Cup campaign.

Both Argentinians have left an enormous mark on international soccer, although their achievements came during different eras, making direct comparisons particularly subjective.

Cristiano Ronaldo's pursuit of 1,000 goals continues

Ronaldo remains an important figure at Al-Nassr , having scored five goals in nine appearances across competitions during the opening stages of the season.

The 41-year-old is scheduled to face Al-Ahli on Thursday, October 15, as he continues pursuing the historic 1,000-goal milestone.

His future with Portugal remains uncertain amid reported disagreements over playing time, but his pursuit of further individual records continues at club level.

Morgan , who has interviewed Ronaldo several times, believes those achievements will remain the strongest evidence supporting his position in soccer's enduring debate.

"Those records will stand the test of time and that is why, for me, he is number one," Morgan concluded.

articles.title: The Cristiano case already has its first victim: “I have resigned”
articles.standfirst: Luís Miguel Henrique, Jorge Jesus's lawyer, left his column at Record over Cristiano Ronaldo's stake in Medialivre, the group that owns the newspaper.
articles.summary: Luís Miguel Henrique, Jorge Jesus's lawyer, left his column at Record over Cristiano Ronaldo's stake in Medialivre, the group that owns the newspaper.
articles.body:
The clash between Cristiano Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus has already had a consequence outside the Portuguese national team. Luís Miguel Henrique , the coach's lawyer, announced that he will stop writing his weekly column in Record because of his relationship with Medialivre, a company in which Cristiano is one of the main shareholders.

Henrique explained that the decision was exclusively his and that he did not receive any pressure to leave the newspaper. His argument: as long as he maintains a dispute with Ronaldo over his role as Jorge Jesus's representative , he does not consider it appropriate to continue being paid by a company in which the footballer has a stake.

It would even be shameful

"Not by anyone's imposition, but by mere and pure personal decision", Henrique explained when announcing his departure. The lawyer maintained that the situation could call his independence into question and that he preferred to end the collaboration rather than create doubts about his opinions.

Henrique also argued that "there is no intellectual independence without financial independence" and considered criticizing a person while maintaining a paid professional relationship with a company in which that person has a stake to be incompatible.

His last column in Record was titled My last dance and was marked by criticism of Cristiano Ronaldo. The lawyer questioned some of the forward's decisions and statements and used an especially harsh tone against the Portuguese captain.

There he argues that, in his view, reason is on the side of the Portuguese coach and admits that he would like the dispute to end differently, although he declares himself “extremely pessimistic” about the direction it has taken.

It also makes clear that he does not want anyone to be able to think that Cristiano, or any other figure, has the capacity to impose any “consequence” on him because of his positions. His argument is that freedom of expression loses value if it is only exercised when it does not entail any personal or professional cost. That is why he understands his resignation as a way of protecting his autonomy.

'"Cristiano Ronaldo, through his actions, his behavior, and his obsession with certain metrics, is achieving what no opponent has managed: ruining our ability to remember all the good he gave us."'

There is an important nuance regarding the group's ownership. Cristiano Ronaldo is not the majority shareholder of Medialivre, but rather one of its main shareholders. CR7 S.A. controls 30% of the capital, while Sorolla S.A. owns 32%. Medialivre owns Record, Correio da Manhã, CMTV, NOW, and other Portuguese media outlets.

Jorge Jesus's lawyer also criticized Cristiano

Henrique's departure comes amid the full-blown crisis between Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus. The conflict began after the match against Norway, when Cristiano remained on the bench despite having warmed up for around half an hour.

According to the footballer's version, he had been told that he would play approximately 30 minutes . In the end, he did not take the field and later left the Portuguese training camp before the match against Denmark. Days later, he publicly explained his version and acknowledged that his decision could have disciplinary consequences.

The Portuguese Football Federation has already opened disciplinary proceedings and ordered a non-automatic preventive suspension against Ronaldo. The procedure was declared urgent and was placed in the hands of the Disciplinary Investigation Commission.

Ronaldo, for his part, left open the possibility of returning to the national team once whatever suspension applies has been served. Jorge Jesus himself also pointed out that the striker could be called up again if he is willing to return.

Thus, a dispute that began within the Portuguese national team has now reached another arena. Jorge Jesus's lawyer decided to leave one of the newspapers in the group in which Cristiano Ronaldo is a shareholder, turning the conflict between them into an issue that also affects the Portuguese media landscape.

articles.title: Soccer coach goes to great lengths to avoid an inappropriate glance at reporter’s cleavage during interview
articles.standfirst: David Oulehla appeared to keep his eyes everywhere but on Sabina Jákšová after his team’s 3-2 loss to Opava
articles.summary: David Oulehla appeared to keep his eyes everywhere but on Sabina Jákšová after his team’s 3-2 loss to Opava
articles.body:
A postgame interview is usually about the score. This one became a test of self-control. After FK Viagem Ústí nad Labem lost 3-2 to SFC Opava, coach David Oulehla spoke with club presenter Sabina Jákšová and seemed to look everywhere except at her.

Jákšová wore a striking white suit over a low-cut brown top . As she asked her questions, Oulehla’s gaze repeatedly shifted toward the floor and off to the side. The clip gives no explanation for his behavior, but viewers quickly read it as an effort to avoid an inappropriate glance.

Fans turned the interview into an eye-contact challenge

Social media users joked that Oulehla was “fighting for his life,” while others praised his apparent restraint. One fan even called for a VAR review to determine whether the coach had looked.

Jákšová joined the club as a presenter last season after its management approached her. She has said she had no previous experience in the role and learned as she went, while trying to feel natural and comfortable on camera.

Oulehla’s team left the field with a 3-2 defeat, but the coach’s careful gaze became the clip’s most replayed moment. For fans, the postgame interview offered an unexpected second contest: the match was over, but the eye-contact challenge had just begun.

articles.standfirst: Ronaldo’s sister claims trust has been damaged after the Al-Nassr star’s shock departure from Portugal’s camp
articles.summary: Ronaldo’s sister claims trust has been damaged after the Al-Nassr star’s shock departure from Portugal’s camp
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo’s future with Portugal has been thrown into doubt after his sister Elma Aveiro suggested that a return to international football looks increasingly unlikely following his reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus .

The 41-year-old forward unexpectedly left Portugal’s Nations League camp during the recent international break after being left on the bench during a 2-1 victory against Norway.

The decision reportedly triggered tensions between Ronaldo and Jesus , raising questions about their relationship and the legendary striker’s future with the national team.

Speaking at a book launch on Wednesday, Aveiro offered a pessimistic assessment of her younger brother’s prospects of returning to the Portugal squad. Jesus was also present at the event, meaning her remarks added another dimension to the developing controversy.

“It’s more likely a no than a yes. I think both [Ronaldo and Jesus] are hurt. It was a situation they experienced, not me, I’m speaking for my brother,” Aveiro said.

“I think it’s a situation that’s stalled, we’ll see what happens. I don’t know, it’s very complicated. When we’re betrayed, it’s very difficult to go back to normal.”

Her comments have intensified speculation about whether Portugal’s record goalscorer could be approaching the end of his international career, despite previously expressing his desire to continue representing his country.

Ronaldo’s international future depends on resolving the dispute

Aveiro also expressed disappointment over what she considers a lack of appreciation for Ronaldo’s contributions to Portuguese football. She believes his achievements deserve greater recognition and admitted that watching her brother experience the controversy has been deeply upsetting.

Her concerns echo those voiced by Ronaldo’s mother, Dolores Aveiro, who reportedly broke down in tears following her son’s dramatic departure from the national team camp.

"For my part, I just hope everything gets resolved for the best. I hope he [Ronaldo] returns and that everything turns out fine. The truth is, that's what we all want. I hope he comes back and everything is sorted out,” said Vitinha .

Ronaldo’s record of 146 goals in 234 appearances underlines his importance to Portugal, making uncertainty surrounding his availability a major talking point ahead of the team’s upcoming fixtures against Denmark and Wales.

Portugal secured victories during the recent international break without their captain, demonstrating that the squad can continue competing in his absence. Nevertheless, his potential return remains a significant issue for supporters and teammates alike.

Tempers flared in the second half of Real Betis’ match against Barcelona after Abde Ezzalzouli scored to make it 2-2. In the buildup, Fermín López had gone down following a tussle, and Lamine Yamal stepped in as players gathered around him.

articles.body:
Without a doubt, October 2026 is shaping up to be one of the most special months of Gilberto Mora’s life. articles.title: "Salvia Messii": a sky-blue and white flower is discovered in Peru and named in honor of the Argentine captain
articles.standfirst: The new species grows in the Peruvian Andes, and its flowers combine white and light blue tones. Scientists decided to name it in honor of Lionel Messi.
articles.summary: The new species grows in the Peruvian Andes, and its flowers combine white and light blue tones. Scientists decided to name it in honor of Lionel Messi.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi received a tribute as unexpected as it was unusual. A new species of plant from the Peruvian Andes was named Salvia messii, in honor of the captain of the Argentine national team. And the choice has a special detail: its flowers feature light blue and white tones, a combination that inevitably recalls the Albiceleste jersey.

The species was formally described by researchers Paúl Gonzáles, Rolando Uría, and Jean Capcha-Ramos and published on October 2, 2026 in the scientific journal Phytotaxa . The study confirmed that it is a new species to science, endemic to the central and southern Andes of Peru.

What is Salvia messii like?

The Salvia messii belongs to the lamiaceae family, the same group to which plants such as mint, basil, and rosemary belong. It is an aromatic shrub that can reach nearly 1.5 meters in height and grows on rocky slopes in the Peruvian Andes.

Known specimens are found between 2,000 and 2,400 meters above sea level, in six localities in the departments of Lima and Ica. Its flowers display a combination of white and light blue that evoked the colors of the Argentine national team and supported the decision to dedicate the species to Messi.

Although the scientific description is recent, the plant did not appear out of nowhere. Records of its populations had existed since 2009, but new expeditions, the collection of specimens, and detailed comparison with other species of the genus Salvia were necessary to confirm that it was a species that had not previously been formally described.

A species already considered endangered

The finding also brings a warning. Salvia messii was only found in six known localities and, due to its restricted distribution, the researchers preliminarily assessed it as an Endangered species (EN).

Among the threats to its habitat are fires, the construction of roads and highways, unregulated tourism, and droughts. Scientists also emphasize the importance of the transitional scrublands surrounding the relict forests of the western Andes, an environment that could still harbor other undescribed species.

Messi also has other species named after him

The tribute of Salvia messii is not the first that Lionel Messi has received within the scientific world. His surname had already been used previously to name different species as a form of recognition of the Argentine footballer's career.

Among them are the spider Acanthogonatus messii, a mygalomorph species recorded in Argentina; the lizard Liolaemus messii, described in Patagonia; and the fungus Cercopemyces messii, whose name was also chosen in honor of the world champion.

The list also includes other organisms and even fossil species that incorporated the surname of the Rosario native into their scientific designation. Salvia messii, however, adds an especially symbolic detail: its flowers combine light blue and white tones, the same colors as the Argentina national team with which Messi reached the summit in Qatar 2022.

Thus, on the rocky slopes of the Peruvian Andes, a new species has just added Messi's surname to the history of biodiversity. A tribute born of science that, because of its colors, also has a distinctly Argentine flavor.

articles.title: Messi won't let go of Cristiano: another brace reignites the race for 1,000 goals
articles.standfirst: The Argentine scored twice in Inter Miami's victory over Atlanta United and reached 936 official goals. Cristiano Ronaldo has 981 and is 19 away from reaching a historic figure.
articles.summary: The Argentine scored twice in Inter Miami's victory over Atlanta United and reached 936 official goals. Cristiano Ronaldo has 981 and is 19 away from reaching a historic figure.
articles.body:
For more than two decades, Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo took their rivalry to numbers that seemed unattainable. Now, in the final stage of their careers, they still have one milestone pending that pits them against each other from afar: becoming the first footballer to reach 1,000 official goals.

Messi scored a brace in Inter Miami's 3-1 victory over Atlanta United and took his tally to 936 official goals . Cristiano Ronaldo, for his part, has 981 and retains a lead of 45 goals.

The math is clear: the Portuguese player needs 19 goals to reach 1,000, while the Argentine captain still needs to score 64 . Although the gap still favors the Al Nassr forward, Messi’s new brace keeps the race open, added to Lionel Messi’s performance in the second quarter of the year.

Messi closes the gap on Cristiano Ronaldo

Inter Miami's captain was decisive in the second half of the match played at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta . He scored in the 56th minute and found the net again just four minutes later to complete his brace. Germán Berterame had opened the scoring before halftime, while Atlanta pulled one back in the final stretch.

The two goals also raised his tally to 25 goa ls in the regular MLS season, in another performance that confirmed his importance in the American team's attack.

The fact fueling the battle with Cristiano lies in both players' scoring pace during 2026. According to the records released after the match, Messi has 40 goals in the calendar year for both his club and the national team, compared to the Portuguese player's 24.

Lionel Messi has a 16-goal advantage in the specified period, although he is still behind in his career total.

The stadium that also holds a World Cup memory

The brace had another ingredient: Messi scored again at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, the venue for the 2026 World Cup semifinal in which Argentina beat England 2-1.

In that match, played on July 15, England took the lead with a goal by Anthony Gordon in the 55th minute.

"The Albiceleste responded in the closing stages: Enzo Fernández equalized in the 85th minute and Lautaro Martínez scored the winner in stoppage time. Messi provided the assist on both plays and was key in sending Argentina through to the final against Spain.

One more victory with Inter Miami, in a stadium that brings back beautiful memories from just a little while ago...

Months later, the Argentine left his mark once again at the same stadium , this time wearing the Inter Miami jersey. His two goals against Atlanta not only contributed to his team’s victory: they also added to his personal tally in a statistical race in which Cristiano Ronaldo still remains ahead.

A race that still has no winner

At 39 years old, Messi continues adding goals and narrowing the gap in one of football’s most closely followed individual comparisons. Cristiano, also in the final stretch of his career, is closer to reaching 1,000, but the Argentine maintains a goal-scoring pace that prevents the race from being considered over.

At 39 years old, Messi continues to tame matches with extraordinary longevity. His brace against Atlanta United raised his official tally to 936 goals and once again narrowed the gap with Cristiano Ronaldo, who leads the race to 1,000 with 981.

articles.title: Truck drives through soccer field during game in Kansas, killing 2 and hospitalizing 11
articles.standfirst: A 6-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man were killed
articles.summary: A 6-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man were killed
articles.body:
A woman drove a truck through a soccer field during a youth game in Kansas on Saturday, killing two people and sending 11 other victims to the hospital, authorities said.

A 6-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man were killed, Wichita Police Capt. Aaron Moses said. The ages of the injured people ranged from 5 to 68.

Moses said the driver, a 34-year-old, was in custody. He did not say whether authorities believe it was intentional.

“We are still working to determine how this happened and why this happened,” he said.

Two children were also in the truck, Moses said.

Police Chief Joe Sullivan said that immediately after the incident, and before first responders arrived at the scene, people “sprang into action” to provide lifesaving assistance to the victims.

“It was truly amazing,” Sullivan said. “But I think it's indicative of the Wichita community.”

Authorities said there was no further public threat.

Mayor Lily Wu advised people to avoid the area during the investigation and said the news was heartbreaking.

“My thoughts and prayers are with everyone affected, especially the children and families involved,” she said via Facebook.

To celebrate seven decades of soccer history, organizers launched a public poll to choose the B.O.A.T. (Best Of All Time). Only legendary players who have won the trophy at least twice during their careers are eligible to take part in this exclusive contest.

Unlike the traditional award, whose winner is determined entirely by an international jury of journalists, this symbolic vote has been opened up to the general public through digital platforms. The unusual voting system requires fans to pay one euro per vote, with users allowed to cast an unlimited number of votes for their preferred candidate.

A commanding lead in the online vote

The first partial results shown by the real-time voting system have produced a striking picture: Cristiano Ronaldo sits comfortably at the top of the poll with a commanding 62% of the total vote. The version of the Portuguese superstar leading the standings is his spectacular 2008 campaign, when he was playing for Manchester United and produced an unforgettable season capped by Champions League and Premier League titles.

Lionel Messi, meanwhile, sits second with 13% of the vote for his extraordinary 2012 campaign, the year in which he set the all-time record of 91 goals in a calendar year. Close behind is Messi's 2023 version with 9%, following his role in leading Argentina to the World Cup title in Qatar.

The enormous gap in favor of the Portuguese forward has drawn considerable attention from outlets such as Clarín, which highlighted how the distribution of votes has benefited Ronaldo's first great European triumph. Messi, on the other hand, is seeing his support divided among the eight different award-winning campaigns represented in the poll.

The rules behind the historic contest and the other legends

The format established by organizers evaluates each individual season in which a player won the award separately, explaining why the players with the most trophies are effectively competing against themselves in different slots. In addition to Ronaldo's 2008 campaign and Messi's 2012 and 2023 seasons, Ronaldo's 2007 (7%) and 2016 (2%) campaigns are also receiving votes.

The exclusive list of 10 legends selected by organizers is completed by some of the greatest names in soccer history: Alfredo Di Stéfano, Johan Cruyff, Franz Beckenbauer, Michel Platini, Marco van Basten, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, Kevin Keegan and Ronaldo Nazário. However, outlets including El Liberal and La Gaceta have focused their coverage almost entirely on the head-to-head battle between the two giants of 21st-century soccer.

The public vote will remain open until midnight on the eve of the main gala on October 26, when the final tally will be locked in. As the countdown continues, fans are taking advantage of their remaining opportunities, paying the required fee to push their idols toward the top of the historic ranking.

Two legends chasing the 1,000-goal milestone

Beyond this symbolic battle in the online polls, both the Rosario-born star and the Funchal native continue to put up remarkable numbers while still playing professional soccer. Despite their ages and having moved away from the center stage of European soccer, both superstars remain locked in another race: becoming the first player in the modern era to officially reach 1,000 career goals.

Cristiano Ronaldo leads that scoring race and is closing in on the historic milestone after surpassing 980 goals in more than 1,300 appearances. The Inter Miami star, meanwhile, continues his pursuit having surpassed 935 goals in more than 1,100 official appearances.

The outcome of the B.O.A.T. poll will serve as a blockbuster appetizer before the new owner of the coveted golden trophy is revealed in the British capital. What is already clear, as reflected by sports media coverage around the world, is that the greatest soccer rivalry of the modern era shows no signs of fading and continues to mobilize millions of fans across the globe.

articles.title: The Times apologizes to Infantino and FIFA for reporting on a "second salary" that did not exist
articles.standfirst: The British newspaper also corrects its reports about a property in Miami and the FIFA president's connection to a company.
articles.summary: The British newspaper also corrects its reports about a property in Miami and the FIFA president's connection to a company.
articles.body:
The Times has published a correction and has apologized to Gianni Infantino and FIFA for a report from last October 13 in which it attributed to the organization's president an alleged " second salary " that had not been disclosed. "This is incorrect. There was no second salary," the newspaper acknowledges in the text released by FIFA.

The correction also addresses the treatment of the expenses and reimbursements received by Infantino. According to the correction, Swiss reporting requirements do not consider those amounts to be remuneration and, therefore, FIFA is not required to include them as such in its annual report .

The British newspaper also retracts its claims regarding a property in Miami . It acknowledges that Infantino did not purchase the property at an allegedly lower value, as it had reported, and corrects the link it had suggested between the official, his family, and Shadi LLC : none of them is the legal owner or beneficiary of that company, nor do they exercise control over it.

'The Times closes its correction with an apology to the president and the organization for the errors . FIFA, for its part, has used the publication to defend its actions and question the spread of those accusations . '

A "concerted and continuous effort" to undermine FIFA

The organization maintains that there is a "concerted and ongoing effort" to undermine FIFA and its president, an allegation that, as it recalls in its statement , it had already made in August . This is the institution's own assessment, which calls on the media for responsibility and careful verification of their sources to avoid publishing and reproducing false and defamatory information .

FIFA says it accepts legitimate scrutiny , but warns that this does not justify amplifying false accusations. In this regard, it announces that it will continue responding "directly and vigorously" to information it considers inaccurate, misleading or false .
